verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
`_read_answer` now reads a word as a number only when `word.isdecimal()`, so `²` or `①` falls through as a name, `parse_harnesses` rejects it, and the prompt loop asks again with the accepted values.
Every value that passes `isdecimal()` also parses with `int()`, so no ValueError path is left.
Diff against HEAD (the change is uncommitted in the worktree): one line in src/kmctl/__init__.py:777 and one new parametrized test at the end of tests/test_plugin.py.
It asserts exit code 0, no exception, that install ran for `["claude"]`, and that stderr has "one of: 1 claude, 2 antigravity".
On the old `isdigit()` code, `int('²')` raises ValueError, so exit code and exception assertions fail.
I confirmed `'²'.isdigit()` and `'①'.isdigit()` are True and `isdecimal()` is False for both.
Row r2: full suite plus integration.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration, r1 and r2 all pass; "stamp green: d5a7e087d6d94a495e8822440404b88490dbfa87d6d0c43bea881f3ee7f080c4".
Consistency: the `_read_answer` docstring ("by number or name; raises PluginError otherwise") still holds.
No other `isdigit` use in src, tests or docs.
